regime_context: The detector shows a broad, non-directional rotation (half the TSX universe eligible) with Gold Miners leading on rank and durability, Silver & Royalties close behind, and energy (Oil & Gas, Base Metals) next. Momentum rank is display-only (rank-IC ~0), and the one validated edge — the absolute-trend gate — did help drawdown control on this market (gate_helps true), so high-durability leaders merit attention not as return forecasts but as lower-risk trend expressions. Macro backdrop is heavily unscheduled/geopolitical (0.87 share), which is coincident context, not a trigger.
emerging_watch: Watch Big Banks (rank 5, durability_bar 0.59, trend-tagged Hurst) for a confirmed leadership handoff away from gold/materials — the condition that would make me pay attention is ZEB.TO breadth expanding above 0.5 AND its durability reading holding above 0.6 over two consecutive weeks while gold's r10 momentum stays negative.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners hold the highest durability_bar (0.73) and full breadth (1.0) among eligible themes, and are not crowded (crowding_z 0.65). The absolute-trend gate is the only validated leg on this market history and favors staying with eligible, high-durability, broad leaders; Gold Miners is the cleanest expression of that. This is a trend-following, vol-aware lean, not a momentum-rank return forecast.
theses.dissent: Gold has already had a strong run and the theme may be late-stage; with momentum rank having no forward edge, leadership persistence is not assured, and a geopolitical headline-driven unwind could hit precious metals hard given the 0.87 unscheduled-news share.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties

theses.dissent: The mean-revert Hurst tag suggests the trend is less persistent than Gold's mixed reading, and its near-identical proxy means it adds little diversification; if gold stalls, silver follows.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags the benchmark by 5% before the check-by date
